items.prose: Acidifying 800 liters of spent lye from the graining kettle with dilute hydrochloric acid precipitated dissolved fatty acid soaps as a floating curd. Skimming off the scum left clear, desalted 'sweet-water' containing 14.5% crude glycerol.

Dosing neutralized sweet-water with 0.5% aluminum sulfate (alum) formed gelatinous aluminum hydroxide flocs. The flocs swept down microscopic protein impurities and color bodies, leaving sparkling, water-clear liquor for evaporation.

Boiling clarified sweet-water under 0.82 bar vacuum reduced its boiling point to 58°C. Evaporating water without atmospheric boiling temperatures prevented thermal decomposition and scorching, producing thick, 82.5% crude glycerin syrup.

Injecting dry 180°C superheated steam through crude glycerin held at 0.94 bar vacuum distilled pure glycerol vapors overhead. Fractionally condensed in air-cooled copper coils, the distillate yielded water-white 99.2% pharmaceutical-grade glycerin.

Picnometer testing of the refined glycerin registered a specific gravity of 1.2612 at 20°C, corresponding to 99.5% glycerol purity. The viscous, sweet-tasting liquid was bottled for compounding medicinal burn salves and ear drops.

Compounding a 60/40 blend of distilled glycerin and deionized water produced non-volatile, non-toxic antifreeze and hydraulic recoil fluid. The solution remained liquid down to -36°C, protecting outdoor intake damper actuators during nuclear winter.

Percolating warm 96% crude glycerin through a three-meter vertical column of granular bone-black charcoal stripped out yellowish carotenoids and choking acrolein traces. The effluent emerged crystal-clear with zero lingering burnt odor.
